A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BEAR/PCSE research on inverse constrained reinforcement learning. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, plots and constraint visualizations, support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original Gridworld and Point Maze experiments, including learning curves and recovered-constraint visualizations in Section 6 and Appendix D.

after.justification: V4 retains original experiments and reports expanded Point Maze comparisons in Figure 4, alongside Gridworld results and constraint visualizations in Section 6 and Appendix E.

M1.justification: The reported exploration signal C_k changes from a clipped local count-based expression in v1 Equation 6 to a rescaled expression incorporating the maximum uncertainty across state-action pairs in v4 Equation 10. Since Algorithm 1 uses C_k for exploration objectives and stopping calculations, this revises a central computational component of both algorithms, although their overall BEAR/PCSE structure remains.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same four stochastic 7-by-7 Gridworlds and the same continuous-state Point Maze navigation task. V4's discussion of transfer to new tasks and offline demonstrations does not introduce evaluated scenarios.

E2.justification: Point Maze Figure 4 expands from BEAR and PCSE in v1 to include epsilon-greedy and maximum-entropy exploration in v4. The Gridworld comparator set remains random, epsilon-greedy, maximum-entropy and UCB exploration; splitting its plots between Figures 3 and 5 does not remove comparators.

E3.justification: The documented environment dimensions, action spaces, stochasticity, 50-step Gridworld and 500-step Point Maze limits, and evaluation metrics are retained. V4's newly disclosed DQN, PPO and action-ranking implementation details do not establish changes to previously used experimental settings.

E4.justification: The Gridworld constraint-learning sequences and Point Maze recovery snapshots are retained, with renumbering and layout changes. Neither version adds distinct ablations, sensitivity tests or distribution-shift evaluations; v4's additional discussions are not new empirical analyses.

E5.justification: Both experimental appendices specify the same five Gridworld random seeds and reporting of means with 68% confidence intervals. V4 does not disclose additional runs, new significance tests or a different uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: V4 Figure 4 adds Point Maze reward and cost trajectories for epsilon-greedy and maximum-entropy exploration, showing higher intermediate costs than PCSE. The displayed BEAR/PCSE trajectories also change, without establishing reruns or a same-setting performance improvement. The principal Gridworld findings and appendix recovery sequences remain.

T1.justification: V4 formalizes minimality through Definition 4.2's minimization of the constraint-violating set, introduces a shifted/rescaled cost construction in Appendix C.4, and revises the error bounds and sample-complexity derivations. The coefficient bound changes from minimum-positive to maximum-positive advantage dependence, and Theorem 5.5 loses its explicit SA factor. Slater's condition is also newly stated. These are substantive mathematical revisions, beyond relocated lemmas.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: feasible-cost-set recovery, analysis of dynamics and expert-policy estimation errors, BEAR and PCSE with tractable sample complexity, and empirical effectiveness in discrete and continuous environments. The revised bounds and expanded qualifications do not replace these headline contributions.

C2.justification: V4 corrects the explanation that equal-reward trajectories departing from the expert must violate constraints, recognizing that they may or may not do so. Sections 7–8 add substantial discussion of hard versus soft constraint transfer, scalability and imperfect experts. Conversely, v1's detailed discussion of unsafe exploration during training and simulation-to-reality concerns is replaced by a generic impact statement.

D1.justification: V4 adds implementation provenance and an Appendix D.3 paragraph describing the DQN expert, density-model counts, PPO exploration for BEAR and action-ranking implementation of PCSE in Point Maze. These improve disclosure without demonstrating that v1 used different implementations. Hardware and existing environment specifications remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V4 substantially expands research positioning through new constraint-inference comparisons, including Hugessen, Kim and Qadri, and an additional related-work appendix covering sample efficiency, misspecification and Bayesian IRL. It more explicitly distinguishes feasible-set recovery from approaches imposing conditions to identify particular constraints.

P1.justification: The abstract and substantial explanatory prose are rewritten. Dynamics/expert estimation moves before error propagation, theoretical statements move between the main text and appendix, limitations are reorganized into the conclusion, and a separate discussion section is introduced. This materially changes the narrative organization.

P2.justification: V4 adopts a two-column main-paper layout, splits the original six-strategy Gridworld plot across Figures 3 and 5, and enlarges and relocates Point Maze panels. Appendix constraint visualizations are substantially resized and repositioned while retaining their underlying images; legends and captions are also revised.

improvement.justification: Clearer definitions, additional Point Maze comparisons and implementation disclosure provide useful gains. However, v4 introduces unresolved inconsistencies in its central guarantees: Appendix C.11 drops the SA factor when summing per-pair counts in Equations 51–52, while Appendix C.13 Equation 55 retains v1's C_k expression despite the revised Equation 10. These issues prevent a reliable judgment that the explanatory and empirical gains produce a net improvement in paper quality.
